script.problem: It has 2 sentences. Explanations are 3 to 5 sentences.

terra.problem: Papa Dorin lives alone on a planet just big enough for his bakery. A neighboring bakery contradicts his world.
The text does not say Hezekiah chose the address wording so nobody would have to guess.
The proclamation invites people to Jerusalem; it does not establish that nobody stayed home.
The plan pleased the king and assembly, but the text does not say nobody grumbled.
The passage does not say the letters were written by hand or that someone's wrist got a workout.
The letter says the people should return so that the LORD may return to those who remain. The explanation changes that into an unqualified statement that He returns to them.
The letter calls the people to come to the sanctuary; it does not establish that they all come.
Saying nothing else is attached to the promise leaves out its stated condition: if they return to Him.
The passage does not say the couriers walked home. 'I think' marks a guess, but it adds an event rather than a possible feeling.
The text reports mockery and says some people came, but it does not establish that the welcome was mostly unwarm.
The text says some came to Jerusalem, not that they walked there.
The text does not say how many came or that there were enough to fill a city.
The explanation is a flat repetition of the answer and adds no distinctive Papa Dorin voice.
The claim that pride would have left the priests and Levites standing still adds an unsupported explanation of their actions.
The passage does not establish that nobody was stomping around.
The text says the unpurified people ate the Passover, not that nobody at all sat out.
Hezekiah's prayer does not name those groups. The preceding verse says many unpurified people were from them, not that all the people covered by his prayer were.
The explanation merely repeats the answer in generic language without Papa Dorin's voice.
The lunch comparison mentions a food occasion outside the permitted cookie-making comparisons.
The assembly agreed to seven more days, but the text does not establish that nobody packed up after the first seven.
The passage does not say the assembly made its decision 'right then, on the spot.'
The text names the groups who rejoiced, including foreigners; it does not say nobody was left outside.
The passage compares the rejoicing with Solomon's days, but it does not say nobody present had seen a celebration like it.
The delivery-service punchline makes the prayer reaching God's dwelling the object of the joke, rather than keeping humor on the human side.
